outOfScope: Global scheduler, role registry or organization workflow graph.
Exactly-once event transport or transactional outbox as a correctness prerequisite.
Deployment, AcceptanceSnapshot or Product QA semantics.
Execution-policy or strategy selection inside the activation boundary.
constraints: Event or queue delivery is not lifecycle, claim or execution authority.
Activation is not strategy selection and is not obligation creation.
Queue, cursor and local backoff state are disposable and reconstructable from canonical work state.
A stale queued hint cannot resurrect invalidated work.
Frontend and Backend independence is governed by exact semantic dependencies, not global development stages.
A durable runtime such as Restate may host activation mechanics but cannot become organizational source of truth or hidden scheduler.
invariants: one domain outage must not block unrelated domain work
queued stale hints cannot resurrect invalidated work
architectureDecisions: event/watch/poll/restart inputs are wake-up hints only; canonical state is re-read on every reconcile
Activation != Scheduling and does not rank multiple actionable work items
activation works on exact projectId/workId/owningDomain keys, never role/stage names
duplicate triggers converge through canonical lifecycle/claim fencing
missed triggers are recovered by domain-specific canonical scans; event queue/cache is disposable
no transactional outbox is required for correctness in D v1
activation never resolves ExecutionStrategy; BB-048 remains the HOW boundary
post-claim/post-release source-obligation currentness is revalidated before execution entry
FE and BE are independently activatable and may use different strategy kinds/versions
implementationSlices: D2: activation -> claim/release -> execution admission handshake
D4: first real Frontend domain + domain-local strategy using same organization/execution contracts
D5: parallel autonomy fixture + activation observations
